summary:
The biggest story is EASD 2026 (Milan, 28 Sept–2 Oct), which has set off a wave of GLP-1 news. The first retatrutide phase 3 results came out on 29 Sept at 22:00 GMT and were picked up by Time, NBC, Scientific American, The Guardian, Ars Technica and The Independent within an hour. "Retatrutide" is also rising on Google Trends US. TRIUMPH-2 (1,152 adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity, 80 weeks) showed average weight loss of up to 20.8% on the 12 mg dose vs 4.0% on placebo, and A1C fell by up to 1.6 points. A knee osteoarthritis sub-study inside TRIUMPH-1 reported up to a 75.8% drop in knee pain vs 40.3% on placebo. Explainer videos will pile up within 48–72 hours, so this is the top priority, and it needs a clear "not approved, don't buy it online" guardrail because counterfeit and research-chemical retatrutide is already making news.

The second cluster is a "data war" between Novo and Lilly, which suits our myth-busting and research-literacy pillars. It has three parts: Lilly's indirect comparison of Zepbound vs Wegovy HD (4.5% more weight loss), Lilly's indirect comparison of orforglipron vs oral semaglutide (1.5% more), and Novo's insurance-claims analysis of stepping up semaglutide vs switching to tirzepatide (heart and stroke events). CagriSema vs tirzepatide 5 mg adds a lesson on how the chosen comparator shapes the result. None of these is a head-to-head randomized trial, and each was sponsored by a drug company. That's the angle.

There are also early, low-competition practical topics:
- **Pen disposal:** safe disposal of used GLP-1 pens, after NYC sanitation needle-stick injuries passed last year's total.
- **Surgery:** the GLIMPSE anaesthesia study (1.41% vs 0.12% regurgitation or aspiration). The angle is to tell your surgical team you're on it.
- **Muscle:** creatine and protecting muscle on GLP-1s.

Myth-busts that are still rising: pancreatic cancer (the Nordic registry found no link) and hair loss. Asthma (ERS, 9 Sept) and the SELECT mediation analysis are peaking and need a differentiated angle.

Everything rejected or held back:
- Any retatrutide sourcing content.
- Any switching or dose-escalation advice.
- The French pregnancy-safety paper, which isn't verified yet.

Sources checked: [Lilly TRIUMPH-2 release](https://investor.lilly.com/news-releases/news-release-details/lillys-triple-agonist-retatrutide-delivered-substantial-weight), [HCPLive TRIUMPH-1 OA/OSA](https://www.hcplive.com/view/retatrutide-improves-weight-loss-knee-osteoarthritis-pain-sleep-apnea-versus-placebo), [BioSpace Zepbound vs Wegovy HD ITC](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/lillys-zepbound-tirzepatide-10-mg-and-15-mg-was-associated-with-more-weight-loss-than-wegovy-hd-semaglutide-injection-7-2-mg-in-a-new-indirect-treatment-comparison), [PR Newswire orforglipron ITC](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/lillys-foundayo-orforglipron-17-2-mg-showed-greater-weight-loss-and-a1c-reduction-than-oral-semaglutide-25-mg-among-adults-with-type-2-diabetes-in-a-new-indirect-treatment-comparison-302891494.html), [HCPLive COMPETE SWITCH](https://www.hcplive.com/view/semaglutide-2-mg-escalation-tied-to-lower-mace-vs-tirzepatide-switch-in-t2d), [Healio REIMAGINE 5](https://www.healio.com/news/endocrinology/20260921/cagrisema-bests-tirzepatide-for-weight-loss-in-adults-with-type-2-diabetes), [MedicalXpress GLIMPSE](https://medicalxpress.com/news/2026-09-glp-drugs-linked-higher-regurgitation.html), [Gothamist sanitation](https://gothamist.com/news/nyc-sanitation-workers-fed-up-with-being-pricked-by-weight-loss-drug-needles), [ScienceDaily asthma](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/09/260909005155.htm), [MedicalXpress hair loss BMJ](https://medicalxpress.com/news/2026-07-glp-diabetes-drugs-linked-higher.html), [NIH alcohol release](https://www.nih.gov/news-events/news-releases/adding-weekly-glp-1-cognitive-behavioral-therapy-further-reduces-heavy-drinking).

candidates.topic: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2: adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight/obesity lost up to 20.8% of body weight on average at 80 weeks (12 mg) vs 4.0% on placebo; A1C down up to 1.6 points (EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'The triple-hormone shot, explained like a friend would': what GLP-1 + GIP + glucagon each do, the exact TRIUMPH-2 numbers with population, timeframe and placebo, why people with type 2 diabetes usually lose less than people without it (and why 20.8% here is notable), plus a clear status line: investigational, not FDA-approved as of late September 2026, and never buy 'retatrutide' online. Hedge the EASD symposium date (Wed Sep 30).
candidates.predicted_peak: 1–5 days (EASD symposium Sep 30, then a creator wave)
candidates.why_now: The embargo lifted 29 Sep at 22:00 GMT. Within an hour Time, NBC, Scientific American, The Guardian, Ars Technica, The Independent and Endpoints all covered it. Google Trends US shows 'retatrutide' at 1,000+ searches and climbing, and the full data are presented at EASD on 30 Sept. Health-creator YouTube explainers of the phase 3 data are still thin.

evidence.signal: TRIUMPH-2: 1,152 adults with T2D + overweight/obesity; −12.7% / −19.1% / −20.8% (4/9/12 mg) vs −4.0% placebo at 80 weeks; A1C up to −1.6 points
Mainstream pickup: 'People with type 2 diabetes lost up to 60 pounds'
Registry record for the TRIUMPH-2 population and design
'retatrutide' trending, ~1,000+ searches

candidates.topic: Retatrutide beyond weight: knee osteoarthritis pain fell up to 75.8% vs 40.3% on placebo (WOMAC pain) in a TRIUMPH-1 basket trial; sleep apnea events also dropped
candidates.angle: 'Less weight, less knee pain?' Explain the nested basket trials (574 people with knee OA and 243 with moderate-to-severe sleep apnea within TRIUMPH-1, 80 weeks). Flag the large placebo response (−40.3%) as the real lesson, and link it to the proven GLP-1 story (tirzepatide already FDA-approved for OSA with obesity). Say clearly that retatrutide is still investigational.
candidates.why_now: The results were released on 29 Sept alongside TRIUMPH-2, but headlines have focused on percentage weight loss. So far the knee and sleep apnea findings appear only in trade press (HCPLive, Medscape, BioSpace). The audience has high rates of knee OA and sleep apnea.

evidence.signal: WOMAC pain −4.5 points (−75.8%) vs −2.4 (−40.3%) placebo; AHI reductions in the OSA basket
'Triple trial triumph', notes that a new safety signal emerged (needs verifying before scripting)
TRIUMPH registrational design: obesity, OSA, knee OA

candidates.topic: Novo vs Lilly 'data war' at EASD: how to read an indirect comparison (Zepbound vs Wegovy HD +4.5%; orforglipron vs oral semaglutide +1.5%; semaglutide 2 mg vs switching to tirzepatide MACE)
candidates.angle: 'Three headlines, zero head-to-head trials.' A research-literacy explainer. It covers what an indirect treatment comparison is (SURMOUNT-1 vs STEP UP, ACHIEVE-3 vs PIONEER PLUS), what a retrospective claims study can and can't show (COMPETE SWITCH), and who funded each one. The takeaway is positive: all of these medicines work, and the right one is a conversation with your prescriber. No 'which is better, switch now' framing.
candidates.why_now: Duelling company releases went out on 29 Sept and are spreading across Benzinga, Yahoo Finance, Investing.com and HCPLive. 'Zepbound vs Wegovy' is already a high-volume evergreen search that this news refreshes. Creators will run 'Zepbound wins' takes, which gives us room to be the calm explainer.

evidence.signal: ITC SURMOUNT-1 vs STEP UP: tirzepatide 15 mg 4.5% more weight loss vs semaglutide 7.2 mg; 20.2% vs 13.7% at 72 weeks
Orforglipron 17.2 mg: 1.5–2.4% more weight loss and 0.3–0.6% more A1C reduction vs oral semaglutide 25 mg (indirect, T2D, 52 wk)
Counter-ITC: oral semaglutide showed greater weight loss vs orforglipron in a different indirect comparison
COMPETE SWITCH claims study: 185,705 escalated vs 23,104 switched; adjusted HR 1.06 for MACE (retrospective, Novo-sponsored)

candidates.topic: Used GLP-1 pens are injuring sanitation workers: NYC reported 57 needle-stick injuries so far in 2026, already above 2025's 51. How to dispose of your pen safely
candidates.angle: A friendly how-to: 'Your pen has a needle in it, even when you can't see it.' Use a sharps container or a heavy plastic bottle labelled 'Sharps – Do Not Recycle', and check local rules. Frame it as a community-care habit, never as shaming users. It's a practical 'life on GLP-1' Short with a clear number in the title.
keywords: how to dispose of Ozempic pen
candidates.why_now: On 29 Sept Gizmodo, ABC News and local TV covered it, and officials are pushing for bigger fines. Disposal searches are practical and evergreen, and almost no health creators have tied them to this news.

evidence.signal: NYC sanitation needle-stick injuries rising, tied by officials to injectable GLP-1 use
57 injuries in 2026 vs 51 in all of 2025 and 37 in 2024
National pickup 29 Sep

candidates.topic: On a GLP-1 and having surgery? GLIMPSE study: regurgitation or aspiration under anaesthesia in 1.41% of GLP-1 users vs 0.12% of non-users (47,039 UK surgical patients, Anaesthesia)
candidates.angle: 'The one thing to tell your surgical team.' Explain why slower stomach emptying matters under anaesthesia and give absolute numbers (about 1 in 71 vs 1 in 830; 19 events total). Say it's observational and doesn't prove cause, and that the societies disagree on what to do. The only action is to tell your surgeon, anaesthetist and prescriber you take it. No stopping or pausing instructions.
candidates.why_now: The Yahoo Health story (29 Sept) and a Medscape 'why can't societies agree' piece are carrying it to consumers. It's a high-intent question for anyone booking surgery or a scope, and the NLM review signal adds to it.

evidence.signal: GLIMPSE: 119 UK sites, 1,348 GLP-1 users; 1.41% vs 0.12% regurgitation/aspiration
Societies disagree on peri-operative GLP-1 management
Consumer pickup 29 Sep

candidates.topic: Semaglutide not linked to pancreatic cancer: regulator-mandated Nordic registry study (97,464 matched pairs, EASD 2026), plus a global propensity-matched cohort showing no pancreatitis signal in T2D
candidates.angle: A reassuring myth-bust with the number in the title: 'Nearly 100,000 matched pairs: no pancreatic cancer signal.' Explain why regulators asked for the study, what 'matched pairs' means, and the limits of registry data. Keep it positive and precise.
candidates.why_now: This is its 4th snapshot at 80–82, and coverage has spread from Medscape to News-Medical (29 Sept). Cancer-fear searches are perennial and this is fresh evidence against them.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide Not Linked to Higher Pancreatic Cancer Risk (28 Sep)
Global propensity-matched cohort: no increased acute pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer in T2D

candidates.topic: CagriSema beat tirzepatide 5 mg for weight loss in type 2 diabetes (12.4% vs 9.1% at 60 weeks, REIMAGINE 5), but the comparator was tirzepatide's lowest maintenance dose
candidates.angle: 'Why the comparator dose matters.' A head-to-head RCT, so better evidence than the ITCs, but the result has to be read against tirzepatide 5 mg, not 15 mg. A1C drops were similar (−1.71 vs −1.67 points). Positive framing: the pipeline is widening options.
candidates.why_now: The topline came out on 21 Sept, EASD coverage has revived it (Pharmacy Times 28 Sept, NewsNation), and the phrase 'outperforms Zepbound' is circulating without the dose caveat.

evidence.signal: CagriSema 12.4% vs tirzepatide 5 mg 9.1% weight loss; A1C non-inferior at week 60 in T2D on metformin/SGLT2i
'CagriSema Tops Tirzepatide 5 mg' (28 Sep)

candidates.topic: Creatine to protect muscle on GLP-1 medicines: what the evidence can and can't say (Clinical Nutrition, Sept 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Protein and lifting first, creatine maybe.' Rank the evidence: resistance training and adequate protein have the strongest support, while creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss is a hypothesis with no GLP-1-specific RCT yet. Hedge. It fits the 'muscle vs fat' double-down pillar. Don't give creatine dose numbers, and advise checking with a clinician if you have kidney disease.
candidates.why_now: A new Clinical Nutrition paper (21 Sept) sits beside a real-world tirzepatide body-composition study (J Diabetes Complications, 25 Sept). 'Creatine' is a hot fitness search, and hardly anyone combines it with GLP-1 muscle evidence.

evidence.signal: Creatine for glucagon-like peptide-1-associated muscle loss
Real-world 6-month tirzepatide effects on body weight and composition

candidates.topic: GLP-1s and hair loss: modest increase (BMJ, 37% higher vs SGLT2 inhibitors, 68% vs DPP-4 inhibitors), mostly non-scarring and likely reversible
candidates.angle: 'Is Ozempic hair loss real?' Give the honest relative numbers with comparators, explain telogen effluvium after rapid weight loss, and say why protein and gentle expectations help. Reassuring: usually temporary. Don't advise stopping, and talk to a clinician if it persists.
candidates.why_now: The Guardian (28 Sept) and Times of India reopened the question after the BMJ study (July) and the NYU genetics paper (Sept 3). Search demand is high and steady.

evidence.signal: 37% higher alopecia risk vs SGLT2i, 68% vs DPP-4i; mainly non-scarring
GLP1R expression linked to 7% higher male-pattern hair loss risk (J Invest Dermatol)

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and alcohol: weekly semaglutide cut heavy drinking days by 13.7 percentage points vs placebo in adults with alcohol use disorder and obesity (RCT)
candidates.angle: The 'food noise' crossover: how GLP-1 acts on the brain's reward system. Use the RCT numbers with population, comparator and small sample, and note that an oral trial missed its craving endpoint. It's promising early research, not an approved use.
candidates.why_now: On 29 Sept Medical Economics carried 'semaglutide cuts heavy drinking', The Atlantic ran a GLP-1 and mental health feature, and the previous snapshot showed Gen X drinking rising. The topic keeps resurfacing.

evidence.signal: Adding weekly GLP-1 to CBT further reduces heavy drinking
RCT: 13.7-point larger drop in heavy drinking days vs placebo; AUD + obesity
Oral semaglutide phase 2: reduced heavy drinking days, not craving/drinks per day

candidates.topic: Semaglutide linked to nearly 40% fewer asthma attacks and ~20% fewer COPD flare-ups (ERS Congress, 80,000+ UK patients with diabetes, observational)
candidates.angle: 'A lung benefit nobody expected, and why it's not proof yet.' Only semaglutide showed the link, not three other GLP-1s. The effect didn't track weight loss. Researchers say don't start a GLP-1 for asthma, because trials are needed.
candidates.why_now: First reported on 9 Sept and still circulating (Medical Dialogues, 29 Sept). It's only worth doing with the 'only semaglutide, not weight-driven' angle.

evidence.signal: Nearly 40% fewer asthma attacks; ERS Congress
Real-world data, up to 40% fewer attacks

candidates.topic: Oral GLP-1 pills are multiplying: orforglipron (Foundayo) now on the market, Novo's $2.6B deal for a once-weekly oral GLP-1/GIP pill (HRS-1596), and safiglipron's placebo-controlled T2D trial (Nature Medicine)
candidates.angle: 'The shot-free future, sorted': how a small-molecule pill differs from a peptide shot, which pills are approved and which are years away (date-hedged), and what 'preclinical' means. No brand promotion.
candidates.why_now: The Hengrui deal (FT, Fierce, 29 Sept), orforglipron data at EASD and the menopause post-hoc snapshot all land together. The 'new weight loss drug like Ozempic' query is showing up in news feeds.

evidence.signal: Novo licenses Hengrui's once-weekly oral GLP-1/GIP HRS-1596, up to $2.6B
Orforglipron: uniform weight loss across menopause stages (post-hoc)
Safiglipron RCT in early T2D: HbA1c up to −1.45% vs placebo over 32 weeks, modest weight effect

candidates.topic: What happens after stopping a GLP-1: 'metabolic whiplash' in 333,000 US veterans with type 2 diabetes (higher heart attack, stroke and death risk after discontinuation, observational)
candidates.angle: 'Keeping the benefit' rather than scaring people. Explain what the data show in veterans with T2D, stress that it's observational, and give the takeaway: any change to treatment is a prescriber conversation. Pair it with what helps results last (protein, strength training, follow-up). No stopping or switching advice.
keywords: what happens when you stop Ozempic
candidates.why_now: Two snapshots at 84 so far. STAT's 'patients vs customers' piece and cheaper telehealth pricing news mean more people are cycling on and off, and interest in 'stopping' searches is sustained.

evidence.signal: GLP-1s increasingly used as 'lifestyle drugs'; churn context
'5 things patients should know about GLP-1 medications' (29 Sep)

candidates.topic: Weight loss explains only ~20% of semaglutide's heart benefit in SELECT (adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight/obesity; European Heart Journal mediation analysis)
candidates.angle: A differentiated angle for a peaking story: 'It's not just the scale.' Cover the other pathways the authors discuss (inflammation, blood pressure, lipids), say what a mediation analysis can't prove, and use the exact SELECT population. Pair it with the Diabetes Care predictors paper.
candidates.why_now: Seven snapshots, flat to declining. Medical Daily (29 Sept) and MUSC's 'ABCs of heart disease now include GLP' keep it alive. A carousel is the best fit.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide and CV risk reduction: mediation analysis of SELECT
Predictors of peak body weight loss with semaglutide in SELECT

candidates.topic: Beware 'retatrutide' sold online: unapproved and counterfeit products linked to serious side effects (a consumer safety explainer)
candidates.angle: Safety-only framing that rides the retatrutide search spike: 'If it's for sale today, it isn't retatrutide from a trial.' Why research-chemical peptides are risky (unknown content, sterility, dose). Link only to regulators, and never name, show or describe sources.
candidates.why_now: The retatrutide headlines will send many searchers toward gray-market sellers. A Korean outlet (Health Chosun, 29 Sept) already reports counterfeit harms. A protective piece serves the audience, but it must never read as a sourcing guide.

evidence.signal: Caution advised buying retatrutide directly; counterfeits linked to severe side effects
'retatrutide' spike

candidates.topic: GLP-1 stomach side effects made easier: new expert review of GI effects across approved shots, pills and pipeline agents (Nutr Clin Pract, Oct 2026) + gastroparesis explainer (Cedars-Sinai)
candidates.angle: 'Nausea, constipation, fullness: what's common, what's not, what helps.' Use evidence-based habits (smaller meals, eating slowly, stopping at full, fluids, fibre, lower-fat meals) and list red-flag symptoms that need a call to your clinician. Positive and practical.
candidates.why_now: A fresh review and the Cedars-Sinai piece (29 Sept) give a new hook to a top-searched GLP-1 question, and it's on the double-down list (side effects).

evidence.signal: Narrative expert review of GI adverse effects of GLP-1 RAs and GIP/GLP-1 RAs, including oral and pipeline agents
What to know about gastroparesis and GLP-1s (29 Sep)
